newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas opens lower, then turns mixed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas opens lower, then turns mixed.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures opened lower, then turned mixed early Tuesday in moderate trade as reports of softer physical prices gave way to technical buying and short covering at support, sources said.
By 1205 EDT, July climbed 1.5 cents to $2.125 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.08. August was 0.6 cent higher at $2.135. Others were narrowly mixed.

"Technically, we bounced off support. We're getting some short covering here, but I think we'll see a lot of people selling if it goes up much more," said one East Coast trader, noting mild weather painted a blead fundamental picture.
With mild weather expected to dominate over much of the country into next week, most traders expect cash and paper markets to remain on the defensive for the near term.
While many technical traders predicted more near-term losses, some expect the market to consolidate here, then rebound with hotter weather forecasts.

"A lot of what happened over the last few days was long liquidation, but the market is very oversold and we hit a lot of people's targets with this selloff," said one Houston-based trader, adding he expected another leg up soon.
Support in July was now seen at today's low of $2.08, with further buying likely at $2.05. Resistance was seen at $2.21, $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Henry Hub prices, which dipped early Tuesday to the $2.08-09 area, rebounded to $2.13 and $2.14 later, still off by about five cents on the day. New York city gate gas also was talked about a nickel lower in the $2.40 area.
NYMEX said 21,793 contracts traded at 1130 EDT. Hub open interest on June 2 fell 1,013 contracts to 196,252.
On KCBT, July firmed 2.5 cents to $2.01, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 11.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on June 2 fell 41 lots to 1,943.
